anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Stale, incomplete, or missing statistical metadata causes systematic cardinality misestimates that misguide the optimizer into choosing inefficient execution plans.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly : Physical or logical corruption inside data pages or index structures breaks key ordering, page links, and row visibility, making persisted structures unreliable and forcing error handling or access-path fall-backs.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database processes consume an abnormally high share of CPU cycles, driving the host into sustained saturation and lengthening all run-queue–related waits.

When these three root causes co-exist, their symptoms overlap and amplify: misestimated cardinalities push the optimizer toward full scans or overly parallel plans that inflate CPU demand; corrupted indexes provoke repeated scan restarts, error logging, or forced heap scans, further compounding CPU consumption; meanwhile the saturated CPU stretches latch acquisition, recovery, and page-verification work, prolonging lock holds and blocking other sessions. End users observe sharp and erratic latency spikes, intermittent wrong-result or "row missing/duplicate" complaints, sudden plan thrash with exploding compile counts, engine errors reporting checksum or logical inconsistencies, and operating-system metrics showing cores pinned at or near 100 % utilization.

Causally, corruption in data or index pages can invalidate row counts that automated statistics collection relies on, accelerating the drift between optimizer assumptions and reality. The resulting bad plans create excessive CPU pressure, which in turn delays or cancels maintenance tasks such as statistics refreshes and online index rebuilds, letting both corruption effects and statistics staleness persist. High CPU also stresses IO and memory paths, increasing the likelihood of additional write-omissions or torn-page events that deepen structural corruption. Thus, each anomaly reinforces the others in a vicious cycle: corruption distorts statistics, bad statistics drive CPU-heavy plans, CPU saturation hampers repair and refresh operations, and the overall database health deteriorates rapidly.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds to wait for more data from a connection before aborting the read.
entry.trigger_condition: The server waits for additional data from a connection longer than net_read_timeout.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
